title: Shiva Tāṇḍava Stotram
intro: A hymn to Shiva as the cosmic dancer, traditionally sung by Rāvaṇa (its last verse calls it daśavaktra-gītam, 'sung by the ten-faced one'). Its Pañcacāmara meter alternates light and heavy syllables, ◡ — ◡ — ◡ —, sixteen to a line, so the words themselves beat like Shiva's ḍamaru.
note: Verses 1 to 13 are the core of the stotra. Verses 14 and 15 appear in some editions and recitations only. Verses 16 and 17 are the phalaśruti, the closing verses on the fruit of recitation. Wording varies slightly between editions; every verse here scans correctly in its meter.
